title: On the convergence of trust region algorithms for unconstrained minimization without derivatives
contribution: Proves lim ||grad F(x_k)|| = 0 for a parameterized family of derivative-free trust-region methods that interpolate F at n+1 points, compute one new F per iteration, maintain geometry by single alpha/beta steps and use no sufficient-decrease test; numerically, symmetric-Broyden quadratic models beat linear ones by more than a factor of 5 up to n=320.
problem_entry: Conn-Scheinberg-Vicente theory keeps geometry conditions (1.5)-(1.6) by model-improvement phases that may cost many F values; can the COBYLA regime of one F per iteration and one replaced point be proved convergent? (pp. 3-4)
key_idea: Interleave cheap geometry-repair steps (alpha: maximize simplex volume when min face distance < alpha*rho; beta: pull in points farther than beta*rho), drop the point with the largest barycentric coordinate after a TR step, and evaluate a TR step only if predicted reduction > gamma * largest observed model error at this rho (pp. 6-8).
assumptions: F bounded below, bounded Hessians of F and of models, exact arithmetic, infinite iterations, nonsingular initial simplex; single never-increased radius rho reduced by exactly 10 and other constants fixed for proof convenience (pp. 2, 5-6, 19).
proof_devices: determinant as simplex volume via Gram-Schmidt: prod sigma_i <= |det D_k| <= prod ||y_i - y_0|| (pp. 9-10)
column-replacement determinant identity |det D_{k+1}| = |theta_t| |det D_k| (p. 10)
Lagrange functions as determinant ratios giving sum |Lambda_j| <= c4, then Taylor expansion inside sum (F-Q)(y_j) Lambda_j = 0 to get ||grad Q - grad F|| <= c3 rho (pp. 11-13)
counting with a monotonically shrinking index set B: every 3n+3 iterations without rho reduction contain a successful TR step (pp. 13-14)
potential Gamma_k = sum ||y_i - y_0|| with per-step increase n*rho and forced beta-step decrease (pp. 15-16)
small determinant forces an alpha step whose gain exceeds worst-case loss over tau_alpha iterations; induction over rho values (pp. 17-19)
explicit success threshold c8 = (19/9 c3 + 5/4 Omega + 5/9 Phi) max[gamma,1] (pp. 20-21)
counterexample F = xi^2 + 3 eta^2 + 0 zeta^2 showing necessity of exact TR steps when model errors vanish (p. 22)
lim inf to lim upgrade by (l, m) index pairs with 10 eps / eps gradient levels and summed decrease contradicting boundedness (pp. 25-27)
experiments: Same algorithm with linear vs symmetric-Broyden quadratic models on trigonometric sum of squares and chained Rosenbrock, n=20..320, 5 random instances each, min-max #F and final infinity-norm error; parameters fixed and theory written before any run; no other solvers (pp. 27-30).
positioning: Credits Conn-Scheinberg-Vicente with most published DFO trust-region theory and reuses their conditions; calls the contrast (one F per iteration vs model-improvement phases) a major strategic difference, in neutral terms; concedes NEWUOA is much more efficient in practice (pp. 2-4).
writing: Theorem in abstract, roadmap at end of section 1, reader told proofs of Lemmas 2-3 can be skipped without losing coherence, each parameter's purpose stated at introduction, algorithm in prose not pseudocode (pp. 1, 4, 6-7, 13, 16, 20).
limits_future: Exact arithmetic; rho never increased causes unnecessarily small steps; test functions may be too easy; future: take NEWUOA's radius adjustment so rho becomes a lower bound, extend to linear (straightforward) and nonlinear constraints (pp. 2, 30-31).

method_links.note: Same points and geometry steps; switching to least-Frobenius symmetric Broyden quadratic models cuts #F by more than 5x up to n=320.

Theory collapses RHO/DELTA to a single never-increased rho; the resolution is lowered only after an unsuccessful TR step and a beta attempt that changes nothing (also evidence for Heuristic 4); Powell plans to restore the two-radius scheme.
Maintaining Z = Y^{-1} in O(n^2) gives alternative steps, face distances and barycentric coordinates by closed formulas.
Parameters untuned and fixed, and theory sections written, before any calculation; surprise and possible weakness of test set stated.
Theory written for a simplified family explicitly less efficient than NEWUOA, not to enable a better code; theory and code decoupled.

transferable: Bound interpolation-model gradient error by writing Lagrange functions as determinant ratios and sandwiching the determinant between prod sigma_i and prod ||y_i - y_0|| (pp. 9-13).

Keep a quantity bounded by a potential with a per-step increase bound plus a periodically forced repair step that removes more than the accumulated increase whenever the potential is large (pp. 15-16).
Use a monotonically shrinking, reset-on-success index set to turn the claim that repairs cannot go on for ever into an explicit count (pp. 13-14).
Drop the interpolation point with the largest barycentric coordinate of the new point; the volume ratio is then exactly that coordinate (pp. 7-8, 10, 17).
Evaluate a TR step only if predicted reduction exceeds gamma times the largest observed model error at the current radius; this replaces a sufficient-decrease test in the proof (p. 7, p. 23).
Fix all parameters and finish the theory before running experiments, and state this in the paper (p. 27).
Tell the reader which proofs can be skipped and structure lemmas so that this is true (pp. 13, 16, 20).

The author had not expected the linear and quadratic models to perform so well when there are hundreds of variables. Perhaps the test functions (8.6) and (8.7) are too easy.

title: Beyond symmetric Broyden for updating quadratic models in minimization without derivatives
contribution: Generalizes the least-Frobenius (symmetric Broyden) model update to a semi-norm with a gradient term theta*||grad Q(v)||^2, implements it in BOBYQA in O(n^2) per iteration via truncated CG, and reports that it rarely helps in practice although it speeds asymptotic convergence in extreme-precision tests.
problem_entry: Symmetric Broyden works well but its projection property only gives vanishing Hessian changes; a positive gradient weight would also give vanishing gradient changes, potentially enabling convergence theory without extra F values, and a 2-variable example shows theta=0 can yield Lagrange gradients of size M (pp. 1-6).
key_idea: Update = least-squares projection in ||Q||_theta = {||Hess Q||_F^2 + 2 theta ||grad Q(v)||^2}^{1/2}, with v = x_{k+1} and theta = eta_k/(2 delta_k) balancing estimated term magnitudes, safeguarded so theta errs small; everything else in BOBYQA unchanged (pp. 2-4, 7-9).
assumptions: No theorem; motivating identity needs quadratic F; experiments use BOBYQA with irrelevant bounds, m in {n+6, 2n+1}; section 5 uses homogeneous quadratics so rescaling avoids underflow; O(n^2) cost assumes m = O(n) (pp. 3-4, 10, 15, 24).
proof_devices: Pythagoras identity for projection onto an affine set of quadratics, giving monotone model error and vanishing changes (p. 3)
closed-form solution of a 3-parameter example via first-order conditions and order-of-magnitude comparison in M (pp. 5-7)
scale-invariance argument: theta must scale like sigma^{-2} under x -> sigma x (pp. 7-8)
moving the theta*g term to the right-hand side of the KKT system so the stored inverse is theta-independent (p. 20)
||G||_F^2 = 2 mu^T A mu proves A PSD, hence I - theta Upsilon_v >= I, strictly convex subproblem and CG error <= gradient norm (pp. 20-21, 23-24)
base-point shift formula giving Upsilon_v products in O(n^2) without an O(n^3) inverse (pp. 21-23)
inexact solve followed by a minimum-Frobenius correction that restores interpolation exactly (p. 25)
experiments: Four versions (m in {n+6,2n+1} x theta in {0,>0}) on 75 problems (trig sum of squares, ARWHEAD with random permutations, chained Rosenbrock with random starts; n=20..320), min-max #F with all baselines rerun on the new code; outliers listed, a surprising cell rerun with 10 more starts; homogeneous quadratics to rho_end=10^-5000 to observe rates and Hessian error; one failure reported and excluded (pp. 10-17).
positioning: Extends his own symmetric Broyden/NEWUOA/BOBYQA line; frames Conn-Scheinberg-Vicente neutrally as theory needing extra F values; uses Broyden-Dennis-More 1973 as the analogy for fast convergence without accurate Hessians (pp. 3-4, 13, 18).
writing: Negative result stated in the abstract; algebraic example before algorithm; candid verdicts (disappointing, puzzled, world's worst); results flagged as not relevant to practical computation; open conclusion that it is too early to reject the idea (pp. 1, 11-14, 17).
limits_future: theta > 0 seldom helps in practice and costs more than BOBYQA's update; no theory proved; section 5 setting artificial; future: automatic choice and adjustment of m, and use of theta > 0 in convergence theory (pp. 3, 13).

method_links.note: Powell tested the alternative norm himself and kept theta=0 for practice; Hessian error barely moves (<0.00025% per update at n=320) while x_fin is accurate, so least-change models work through curvature memory; resolves the unverified remark in Method 3 about other norms.
rho_end is a crude accuracy control; BOBYQA requires at least three new F values per rho before reducing it, which Powell notes excludes superlinear convergence.
On ARWHEAD, m=n+6 often needs far fewer F values than m=2n+1.
Main difficulty was an accurate O(n^2) implementation; rescaling device against underflow; accuracy loss when ||y_j||/Delta_k > 10^7; stable factored updates retained.
Full min-max ranges, raw outlier values, extra runs to confirm a surprise, explicit failure report.
Exactly one change (theta) inside unchanged BOBYQA; theta=0 recovers the predecessor.
BOBYQA had been sent by e-mail to about 200 people; extension keeps the same user data.

transferable: Use a scale-invariance calculation (x -> sigma x) to decide how a free weight must depend on the current length scale instead of tuning a constant (pp. 7-8).
Guard adaptive parameters against self-reinforcement: estimate the next theta from the theta=0 solution and damp with max[0.7*old, new] (p. 9).

Move a parameter-dependent term to the right-hand side of a KKT system so a stored factored inverse stays valid, then solve the small fixed-point system by truncated CG with an a posteriori error bound (pp. 20-21).
After an inexact solve, add the minimum-norm correction that restores hard constraints exactly (p. 25).
For rate experiments on homogeneous functions, store (sigma, 10^sigma x) and rescale when the radius drops, enabling accuracy far beyond floating-point range (p. 15).
When one table cell is surprisingly good, rerun that cell with 10 extra random instances and report both ranges (p. 12).
Show the raw values behind a suspicious min-max range so readers can tell an outlier from a spread (p. 12).
Put the negative result in the abstract and end with what could change the verdict (pp. 1, 13).

quotes.text: A simple example suggests that the extension does bring some advantages, but numerical experiments on three test problems with up to 320 variables are disappointing.
Therefore, although BOBYQA achieves good accuracy in xfin, it may be the world’s worst procedure for estimating second derivatives of objective functions.

title: On fast trust region methods for quadratic models with linear constraints
contribution: Records the design of LINCOA's O(n^2)-per-iteration step for a quadratic model under linear constraints and a trust region (active sets with near-active constraints plus projected truncated CG), proves finite termination of the procedure, and documents why Krylov-subspace steps and boundary searches were rejected.
problem_entry: LINCOA must find a feasible point with small model value under linear constraints and a trust region in O(n^2) operations for hundreds of variables; model Hessians are inaccurate, so exact O(n^3) subproblem solves are not worthwhile (pp. 1-3).
key_idea: Active-set truncated CG in the original variables with projected gradients; near-active constraints within eta2*Delta define the first direction (TOLMIN device) so blocked steps are long; active constraints imposed on increments; active set changed only away from the TR boundary; Krylov and boundary searches rejected after trial (pp. 8-25).
assumptions: F computable at infeasible points; feasible start; possibly indefinite model Hessian available only via O(n^2) matvecs; model updating and model iterations out of scope; no outer convergence theorem (pp. 2-4, 30).
proof_devices: finite CG per active set: failed relative-decrease test forces geometric growth of the model reduction, bounded on the trust region (p. 18)
finite number of active-set changes: each change multiplies the model reduction by at least (1 + eta1 eta2 / 4), using the guaranteed step length > eta2 Delta (pp. 18-19)
sign lemma from QP multipliers: d_perp^T grad Q = sum lambda_j r_j <= 0 (pp. 20-21)
hand-built 2-D and 3-D counterexamples with exact numbers exposing Krylov failures (pp. 11, 14-16)
shifted trust-region centre and radius after fixing an active set away from x_k, explaining when Krylov is unsuitable (pp. 27-28)
Krylov dominance over CG-with-boundary-search in the unconstrained case (pp. 25-26)
experiments: Points-in-triangle problem (3n/2 linear constraints, several local minima), n=10..320, 5 random starts, NPT=n+6 and 2n+1; LINCOA with vs without boundary searches; #F, #TRI and histogram of Hessian-vector products per iteration; boundary searches cost +27%/+7%/+35% #F in key rows (pp. 23-25).
positioning: Assembles classical components (Gill-Murray active sets, Goldfarb-Idnani, More-Sorensen, Conn-Gould-Toint, own TOLMIN and NEWUOA) and his 2013 paper on model accuracy; no competing DFO solver discussed; states it is not a description of LINCOA (pp. 3, 7-10, 16, 29-30).
writing: Abstract announces rejected techniques; paper structured as a decision record (attractive idea, counterexamples, relief, supporting tables, decision in 2013); worked examples to four decimals; motive for reporting failures stated in the last paragraph (pp. 1, 4, 15-16, 25, 30).
limits_future: Model update and model iterations out of scope; one test family; LINCOA undocumented; future: theta-regularized Krylov step to restore monotonicity, Krylov possibly useful when active-set changes occur at the TR centre (pp. 26, 29-30).

method_links.note: Whole subproblem design driven by an O(n^2) budget; named device against tiny steps (eta2*Delta from TOLMIN); cancellation in the projected gradient shown harmless.
LINCOA adds active sets to NEWUOA's truncated CG and reuses TOLMIN's near-active set; NEWUOA's boundary search tried and removed rather than carried over.
Mechanism argument for low-accuracy NPT=O(n) models (sub-level set avoids worse interpolation points); small NPT a welcome surprise.
Test problem with known local minima, both reported with F values; target regime stated, small n weighted less (also Heuristic 5).
Some iterations may evaluate infeasible points, including equalities written as two inequalities.

transferable: Impose active constraints on step increments rather than positions, so nearly active constraints join the active set without a tiny step onto them (p. 9).

Build the first search direction from all constraints within eta2*Delta via a small QP, so any blocking constraint allows a step >= eta2*Delta; this also powers the finiteness proof (pp. 9-10, 18-19).
Prove finiteness of a nested procedure by showing each restart multiplies a bounded achieved reduction by a fixed factor > 1 (pp. 18-19).
When an attractive method misbehaves, find the smallest exact example that isolates the failure, then the geometric reason that predicts it (pp. 14-16, 27-29).
Report inner-solver cost as a histogram of expensive operations per outer iteration alongside #F (p. 24).
Report the different local minima found from different starts with their F values (p. 23).
Write a design paper as a decision record: what was tried, what killed it, when the decision was taken (pp. 4, 16, 25, 30).

The reason for giving so much attention to failures of the Krylov method is that our findings may be helpful to future research.
